contracts.rule: Editing a generation graph bound to a slot moves no task hash, so it is reported as drift: the output node's authored hash differs from its last completed run's, or the node never ran and the graph is not the default one. A run redraws a drifted planned task once.
contracts.prevents: A `done` record keeping a picture the edited graph would no longer draw for the life of the project, or a slot redrawn on every run whether or not anyone edited its graph.
contracts.detail: A bound graph runs the slot, and the graph is the slot's runner rather than part of what the slot is, so editing it never moves the task hash; the difference shows as drift. `graphFacts` summarises each bound slot as a `BoundGraphFact`, and `boundDrift` decides it; `solve` reports it on `SlotState.drift` when the facts carry `graphs`. `graphDrift` recomputes each Output node's authored hash and compares it against the journal's last `done` record for that node, for the report. `requeueDrifted` (`@vn/scheduler`, through `driftedTasks`) returns every planned `done` or `needs_human` task whose bound graph has drifted to `pending`. It runs once per run, before the wave loop, and `RunSummary.redrawn` names the tasks it requeued. `vngen cost` prices a redraw from that same decision: `boundSlotsToDraw` reads the task graph the dry run left and prices a drawn bound slot whose task is `pending`, so the estimate covers both arms. `vngen status` lists what `graphDrift` reports, the edited arm alone, whatever the task. A graph bound to a slot the built-in runner already drew has no `done` record for its output, so `graphDrift` reports nothing for it, but the slot is still drifted unless `isDefaultGraph` finds the graph equivalent to `defaultSlotGraph` for the slot, which draws what the built-in runner drew. That comparison uses authored hashes, so a default graph whose nodes were only moved or joined by unconnected nodes still counts as the default. The redraw writes the output's first `done` record, so it is asked for once. Drift is measured on `authoredHashes`, which reads each host-seeded input (the derived prompt, the task refs) as though nothing had been seeded onto it, and not on the task's own `nodeHash`, which includes the seeding and would report drift after every run. A successful redraw writes the graph's new authored hash into the journal, which clears the drift; that holds for a redraw the executor resumed from a cached answer too, because a node that resumes while its latest `done` record carries stale hashes writes a fresh `done` record under the current ones. Without that record an edit that leaves the output unchanged (an empty `{varC}` added to a template) would keep the slot drifted and requeue it on every run. A failed redraw writes no such record, so the failure goes to `requeueFailed` and its own attempt budget rather than being requeued here forever. The requeue happens at run time rather than at the graph write, because undo excludes `vngen/state/`: undoing a graph edit restores the authored hash, so the drift disappears before anything is redrawn. Editing prose is the opposite case; see `script.proseDriftReported`.

contracts.rule: A node in a generation graph is addressed by its key, the chain of ids from the root (`3/7` for node 7 inside instance 3), never by its id alone. The hashes, the journal, the executor's targets, the cost walk and every `gengraph.*` command's `node` prop use it.
contracts.prevents: A node inside a group instance sharing its id with a root node, since every graph's ids start at zero, so the two would share a hash, a journal record or a command target.
contracts.detail: A root node's key is its id, so keys in a graph with no groups are unchanged and a journal written before groups existed still matches its nodes. Every `node` prop on a `gengraph.*` command resolves through `resolveNodeKey`, so the pane writes an instance's override as `gengraph.setProp` on `<instance>/<id>`, and the agent's whole-graph rewrite keeps an instance under `group: <ref>`.

contracts.rule: An edit inside a group instance can only override a value; `decideGenEdit` refuses a structural edit there with the sentence `structuralEditsRefused` gives. Structural edits go to the group's definition, written as `vngen/work/graphs/lib/<ref>.json`.
contracts.prevents: One instance's wiring silently diverging from the definition every other instance shares, so editing the definition no longer describes what that instance runs.
contracts.detail: Every `gengraph.*` editing command reaches a definition through its `group` prop. The renderer only reads the definition file; it never writes it.

contracts.rule: Renaming a node type's socket or prop needs a migration in the same commit: bump the type's `typeVersion` and add a `NodeMigration` step that lands on it. `migrateGraphJSON` replays the renames over a file's JSON before `readGraphFile` deserializes it.
contracts.prevents: A file written before the rename loading with the old key as an orphaned socket, its link reaching nothing visible and the renamed key at its default, so the wiring is lost silently and the changed hash redraws the slot.
contracts.detail: path.ux reconciles a loaded node against its definition by key. The replay moves sockets, props, links, a group's forwarded rows, and the `{name}` tokens a template embeds, which puts the node back on the hash a freshly created one would have. `registerGenNode` refuses a migration whose targets name nothing on the class or whose last step stops short of the declared `typeVersion`. A file keeps its old keys until something writes it back, so a migration stays in place rather than being deleted a release later.
